- When sentiment is consistently high (≥0.8) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next period.
- If model shows sharp upward spike followed by high sentiment, it often overshoots; cap peak forecasts at +5% above recent 7-day average.
- When sentiment is low (≤0.3) and price is trending down, model often underestimates; add 1–2% to forecast to avoid premature mean reversion.
- Model frequently overreacts to short-term sentiment shifts; apply smoothing filter (e.g., 3-period moving average) to forecast if sentiment volatility > 0.2.
- For 30-day horizon, if true outcome deviates >5% from 14-day moving average, adjust forecast to align with recent 7-day trend, not 30-day trend.
- If sentiment history shows alternating high/low cycles, model tends to lag; forecast should be 1–2 days ahead of sentiment peak or trough.
